title: SelfConcordantBFGS.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Strictly convex minimization on an open convex domain D ⊆ ℝ^d, with positive-definite Hessian everywhere and an attained minimum. No uniform strong-convexity constant is assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Returns the exact gradient at x + αv, including the initial gradient through a zero-direction query.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Bundled Armijo–weak-Wolfe line-search oracle: for every strict descent direction it returns α > 0 and the endpoint gradient, preserving membership in D and satisfying the two line-search inequalities with 0 < c1 < c2 < 1. Each entire reply costs one call; internal function or gradient evaluations are not counted separately. Replies may depend on history and correlated random seeds, but every reply must satisfy these exact conditions.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SelfConcordantBFGS.lean: spec.valid, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Oracle, executeWithTrace

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Standard self-concordance: |D³f(x)[h,v,v]| ≤ 2√(D²f(x)[h,h])D²f(x)[v,v]. Three derivatives exist, the Hessian is positive definite, and every domain-restricted sublevel set is closed in the ambient space. No global gradient or Hessian Lipschitz bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is ℝ^d, represented by Fin d → ℝ.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information consists only of d, x0, and positive-definite B0. Hidden analysis parameters satisfy Δ ≥ f(x0) − min_D f, Φ0 ≥ 2 log det(B0 + H0) − log det B0 − log det H0 − 2d log 2, and ε > 0, where H0 = ∇²f(x0). The line-search constants c1,c2 are also absent from Public.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SelfConcordantBFGS.lean: Public, Params, mismatch, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The final output must belong to D and satisfy f(output) − f(xstar) ≤ ε for a global minimizer xstar ∈ D.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the final-output objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the execution law, after the supplied fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The objective class and line-search conditions are classical, but the complexity model packages an entire admissible line search and endpoint gradient into one oracle call, with a specific log-determinant initialization bound.

descriptionHtml:
Self-Concordant Minimization with BFGS

We consider minimizing f:Rd→R over an open convex set D⊆Rd, where d≥0 is an integer. On D, the function is self-concordant with positive definite Hessian, has closed sublevel sets, and attains its minimum at x⋆∈D. BFGS starts from a given x0∈D and positive definite matrix B0, with bounded initial objective gap and Hessian mismatch. The oracle returns a feasible Armijo–Wolfe step and its endpoint gradient. For ε>0, the goal is a last iterate x¯∈D satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Df(x). We use the coordinate space Rd with its supremum norm and the pairing u⊤v=∑i=1duivi. The gradient denotes the coordinate representation of the derivative, so df(x)[v]=∇f(x)⊤v. Write H(x)=∇2f(x) for the Hessian matrix. The algorithm receives only d, x0, and B0; the parameters 0<c1<c2<1, Δ≥0, Φ0≥0, and ε>0 may enter the call budget, with c1,c2 also specifying the oracle conditions.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Domain and self-concordance). The set D is open and convex. The function f is three times Fréchet differentiable on D. For every x∈D, every nonzero v∈Rd, and every h∈Rd, v⊤H(x)v>0,|∇3f(x)[h,v,v]|≤2h⊤H(x)hv⊤H(x)v. For every a∈R, the set {x∈D:f(x)≤a} is closed in Rd.

Assumption 2 (Minimizer and initialization). The given point satisfies x0∈D, and B0∈Rd×d is symmetric positive definite. There exists x⋆∈D such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for all x∈D,f(x0)−Δ≤f(x)for all x∈D. For positive definite matrices B,H, define Ψ(B,H)=2log⁡det(B+H)−log⁡detB−log⁡detH−2dlog⁡2. The initial Hessian mismatch satisfies Ψ(B0,H(x0))≤Φ0.

Assumption 3 (Armijo–Wolfe oracle). A query consists of a point x∈D and a direction v∈Rd satisfying ∇f(x)⊤v≤0. The reply (α,g+)∈R×Rd satisfies x+αv∈D,g+=∇f(x+αv). If ∇f(x)⊤v<0, it also satisfies α>0,f(x+αv)≤f(x)+c1α∇f(x)⊤v,c2∇f(x)⊤v≤(g+)⊤v. These conditions hold for every query history and every realization of the oracle randomness. Replies may depend on that history, and randomness across calls may be dependent. For a direction with zero directional derivative, only endpoint feasibility and the exact endpoint gradient are required.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze BFGS with the given initial matrix B0. The first oracle call queries (x0,0) to obtain g0=∇f(x0), leaving x0 and B0 unchanged. Thereafter, for k≥0, the method queries (xk,vk) and receives (αk,gk+1), with vk=−(Bk)−1gk,sk=αkvk,xk+1=xk+sk,yk=gk+1−gk. The Hessian approximation is updated by Bk+1=Bk−(Bksk)(Bksk)⊤(sk)⊤Bksk+yk(yk)⊤(yk)⊤sk. Each scalar reciprocal in this formula is defined to be zero when its denominator is zero; the matrix inverse is likewise defined to be the zero matrix when singular. Thus the recurrence also specifies the update at a stationary point.

Each oracle call returns the step and endpoint gradient together. After N≥1 calls, including the initialization call, the output is the last iterate x¯=xN−1; with zero calls it is x¯=x0. The required accuracy is x¯∈D,f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
On an open convex D⊆Rd, f has three derivatives, positive-definite Hessian, closed sublevel sets, and a minimizer x⋆∈D, with |D3f(x)[h,v,v]|≤2D2f(x)[h,h]D2f(x)[v,v]. Assume x0∈D, B0≻0, initial gap at most Δ, mismatch at most Φ0, and 0<c1<c2<1. The setup requires unmodified BFGS; each oracle call returns an admissible weak-Wolfe step and exact gradient. Target: f(xT)−f(x⋆)≤ε for every admissible oracle realization.

(2) BFGS (Jin and Mokhtari 2025), Thms. 3.1, 3.3, 4.3; App. D O(1+min{Ψ(B¯)+(1+D0)2ℓ,Ω+ℓ,Ω+ℓlog⁡(2+ℓ/Ω)}) Wolfe calls; fixed c1,c2, c1<1/2. Restricted to strongly self-concordant objectives on Rd.

(1): Scope extends to standard self-concordance, including barriers. For B0=aH⋆, a≫1, mismatch dependence becomes dlog⁡a instead of linear in a (other parameters fixed). Allows c1≥1/2.

For B0≈H⋆, 1≤d≪Δ, log⁡(1/ε)≲dΔ2: O(dΔ2) versus the O(Δ3+log⁡(1/ε)) bound (93); not dominance over the displayed minimum.

source:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sqrt
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.NonsingularInverse
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PosDef
import LongTails.Setups.LinearPredictorBFGS
import LongTails.Template

open Set Matrix

namespace LongTails.Setups.SelfConcordantBFGS

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Vec (d : ℕ) := Fin d → ℝ

structure Public where
  d : ℕ
  x0 : Vec d
  B0 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

structure Params extends Public where
  c1 : ℝ
  c2 : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  Φ0 : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  D : Set (Vec p.d)
  f : Vec p.d → ℝ

def hessMatrix {d : ℕ} (H : Vec d →L[ℝ] Vec d →L[ℝ] ℝ) : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
  Matrix.of fun i j => H (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1)

noncomputable def mismatch {d : ℕ} (B H : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2 * Real.log (det (B + H)) - Real.log (det B) - Real.log (det H) - 2 * d * Real.log 2

def SelfConcordantOn {d : ℕ} (D : Set (Vec d)) (f : Vec d → ℝ) (Df : Vec d → Vec d →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (D2f : Vec d → Vec d →L[ℝ] Vec d →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (D3f : Vec d → Vec d →L[ℝ] Vec d →L[ℝ] Vec d →L[ℝ] ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x ∈ D, HasFDerivAt f (Df x) x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ D, HasFDerivAt Df (D2f x) x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ D, HasFDerivAt D2f (D3f x) x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ D, ∀ v, v ≠ 0 → 0 < D2f x v v) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ D, ∀ h v, |D3f x h v v| ≤ 2 * √(D2f x h h) * D2f x v v) ∧
  (∀ c : ℝ, IsClosed {x | x ∈ D ∧ f x ≤ c})

structure State (d : ℕ) where
  x : Vec d
  g : Vec d
  B : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ
  started : Bool

noncomputable def direction {d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (g : Vec d) : Vec d :=
  -(B⁻¹ *ᵥ g)

noncomputable def bfgs {d : ℕ} (x0 : Vec d) (B0 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) :
    Algorithm (Vec d × Vec d) (ℝ × Vec d) (Vec d) where
  State := State d
  initial _ := ⟨x0, 0, B0, false⟩
  query st := (0, (st.x, if st.started then direction st.B st.g else 0))
  update st r :=
    if st.started then
      ⟨st.x + r.1 • direction st.B st.g, r.2,
        LinearPredictorBFGS.bfgsUpdate st.B (r.1 • direction st.B st.g) (r.2 - st.g), true⟩
    else ⟨st.x, r.2, st.B, true⟩
  output st := st.x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Vec p.d × Vec p.d
  Reply p := ℝ × Vec p.d
  Output p := Vec p.d
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.c1 ∧ q.c1 < q.c2 ∧ q.c2 < 1 ∧ Matrix.PosDef q.B0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Φ0 ∧
    0 < q.ε
  admissible q I oracle :=
    IsOpen I.D ∧ Convex ℝ I.D ∧ q.x0 ∈ I.D ∧
    ∃ Df D2f D3f, SelfConcordantOn I.D I.f Df D2f D3f ∧
      (∃ xstar ∈ I.D, ∀ x ∈ I.D, I.f xstar ≤ I.f x) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ I.D, I.f q.x0 - q.Δ ≤ I.f x) ∧
      mismatch q.B0 (hessMatrix (D2f q.x0)) ≤ q.Φ0 ∧
      (∀ history x v seed, x ∈ I.D → Df x v ≤ 0 →
        x + (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).1 • v ∈ I.D ∧
        (∀ w, Df (x + (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).1 • v) w =
          (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).2 ⬝ᵥ w) ∧
        (Df x v < 0 →
          0 < (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).1 ∧
          I.f (x + (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).1 • v) ≤
            I.f x + q.c1 * (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).1 * Df x v ∧
          q.c2 * Df x v ≤ Df (x + (oracle.answer history (0, (x, v)) seed).1 • v) v))
  successful q I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.D, (∀ x ∈ I.D, I.f xstar ≤ I.f x) ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), output ω ∈ I.D ∧ I.f (output ω) - I.f xstar ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p algorithm := algorithm = bfgs p.x0 p.B0

end LongTails.Setups.SelfConcordantBFGS
